issues.legal_issue: The statutory restrictions on holding land by specified entities do not apply to land that qualifies as plantation land.
material_facts: The landowners claimed that a substantial part of an estate purchased by a partnership firm was plantation land.
The Tribunal had treated a major part of the estate as plantation land, but the sale deed described a large area as forest land.
issues.conclusion: If the Tribunal’s finding that the land qualifies as plantation land is correct, the statutory restrictions on holding land by specified entities do not apply to that land.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 2(18), 79-B and 104 of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, land includes forest and plantation land, while the restrictions in Section 79-B do not apply to plantation land. No earlier cases were relied on for this proposition.

predicates.land_ceiling_proceeding: An authority is determining whether land held by a person or entity exceeds a statutory ceiling.
predicates.land_qualifies_as_plantation: The land is used principally for cultivating plantation crops or for purposes included in the legal meaning of plantation land.
predicates.plantation_land_exempt_from_holder_restr: The restrictions on holding land by specified entities do not apply to the plantation land.

issues.definition: When a ceiling proceeding concerns land that qualifies as plantation land, the restrictions on holding land by specified entities do not apply to that land.

issues.legal_issue: A ceiling determination cannot stand where the inquiry inadequately examines whether land described as forest became plantation land and how land acquired by a firm came to be held individually.
material_facts: The sale deed described a large tract of the estate as forest land, while the landowners claimed that much of the estate was plantation land.
The authorities had not adequately examined how the forest land became plantation land.
The estate had been purchased by a partnership firm, but the landowners had not identified a legal instrument by which the firm’s property became the partners’ individual property.
The State challenged the adequacy of the inspection, and the Court found that the authorities’ scrutiny was inadequate given the size and nature of the estate.
issues.conclusion: The Court set aside the Tribunal’s orders and the challenged High Court judgments and directed a fresh proceeding, leaving the authorities to examine the proper procedure and the relevant land-status and ownership questions.
issues.legal_principle: A ceiling determination must be based on adequate examination of material factual questions affecting the land’s status and ownership. The Court applied Sections 66, 79-B and 104 of the Karnataka Land Reforms Act, 1961, and set aside the determinations because the necessary factual examination had not been undertaken. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: land_ceiling_proceeding and large_forest_area_described_in_transfer and plantation_status_unexplained and ownership_transition_unexplained and inadequate_factual_scrutiny

predicates.land_ceiling_proceeding: An authority has determined whether land held by a person or entity exceeds a statutory ceiling.
predicates.large_forest_area_described_in_transfer: A transfer document describes a substantial part of the land as forest land.
predicates.plantation_status_unexplained: The record does not adequately explain or establish how land described as forest land came to be treated as plantation land.
predicates.ownership_transition_unexplained: The record does not adequately explain how land acquired by an entity came to be held individually by its members or associates.
predicates.inadequate_factual_scrutiny: The authorities did not adequately investigate material facts affecting the land’s status or ownership.
predicates.ceiling_determination_set_aside_and_refe: The existing ceiling determination is set aside and the matter is sent for a fresh inquiry.

issues.definition: When a ceiling proceeding involves substantially described forest land, unexplained plantation status and ownership transition, and inadequate factual scrutiny, the existing determination is set aside and the matter is referred for a fresh inquiry.
